findings.source_issue: k is defined as the current maximum index, then assigned to newly created formulas. When another formula already retains index k, the promised distinctness of indices fails.
findings.minimal_treatment: Define k as one plus the current maximum, leaving the displayed k/k+1 patterns unchanged, with disclosure.

findings.source_issue: The fallback c0 need not belong to the assigned constant set C. For example, an initial constant set containing only c1 and no function symbols may exhaust its terms, then acquire c0 in a sequent without adding c0 to C. This contradicts the later invariant and can invalidate a fresh-constant choice.
findings.minimal_treatment: Reuse the first constant already in nonempty C instead, preserving the invariant, with disclosure.
